answer: A sybil farm's power is fungibility: every fake identity can do every job, so one operator covers the whole map. End fungibility. Each epoch, an identity must claim one narrow ridge of work — a single domain, ledger, or proof type — and only work on that ridge counts; all else earns nothing. A farm must either crowd every identity onto one ridge, where the pile-up is obvious, or spread thin across ridges it cannot credibly work. A raven can perch on only one ledge at a time; standing should follow the perch actually held, not the flock claimed.
